statement_summary: One group program aligned to CSF 2.0 meeting each division's obligations
Group CISO accountable; division leads named; CySO and per-facility alternates designated in writing
Annual SP 800-30 risk analysis per division with roll-up; feeds Cybersecurity Assessments
Risk acceptance authority by level; High safety risks must be treated
Division supplements may not weaken group policy; re-align within 90 days; annual attestation
Each division documents inherited common controls each year
Affiliate separation: no cross-division customer data or preference without legal approval
Sanctions, including withdrawal of access for longshore workers and vendors
Third parties: security review, notification terms, jump host access, procurement criteria
FCI only inside the CMMC Level 1 scope; CUI only in an approved SP 800-171 environment
Annual independent assessment; Plan auditors independent of the measures
Exceptions written, rated, approved and time-limited; compensating controls in the Plan
Retention: 6 years for program records; 2 years for facility security records; 6 years for CMMC artifacts
AI systems registered and approved; safety case for equipment-moving AI
Unique identities on IT and OT; no shared accounts
Least privilege; cross-division access approved by the data owner, not the requester's manager
MFA for all workforce IT access and remote OT; phishing-resistant for administrators
Password strength; default passwords changed before use
Lockout after 5 failed attempts; idle locks; shift-end sign-out
Service accounts owned, governed, rotated and certified
Same-day termination; longshore IDs disabled on lapse; weekly reconciliation of local accounts
Quarterly certification including privileged, service and vendor accounts
Just-in-time privileged access through PAM
Vendor and integrator access only through the jump host; no modems or exposed access; justification for remote OT
Break-glass accounts per critical system, tested quarterly
MFA offered on external portals; required for administrators and truckers by set dates
Group IR plan, division annexes and a Cyber Incident Response Plan per facility
One severity scale; cross-division and OT incidents Severity 2 or higher
Report suspected incidents immediately, within 1 hour
Immediate report to the FBI, CISA and the COTP for each affected facility; NRC and FSP reporting
Other notices per the group matrix: DoD 72 hours, 52.204-25, state laws, contracts
Facts to the disclosure committee; Form 8-K Item 1.05 within four business days of a materiality determination
Safe state for OT and life-safety systems; joint restart approval
Preserve evidence; 90 days for covered defense information
No ransom without approvals, OFAC check and law enforcement notice
Two cyber drills and one exercise per facility each year; annual cross-division tabletop
Incidents logged; records kept 2 years
Lessons learned within 30 days into registers and Plans
Classify data and record locations in the data inventory
SSI marked, stored and shared under 49 CFR part 1520
Terminal customer data not shared across divisions
FCI only in scope; CUI only in an approved environment; same-day report of stray CUI
Encryption in transit and at rest; no plain FTP after 2026-12-31; OT compensating controls
Printed release and dangerous cargo lists controlled and shredded
Media sanitized or destroyed with certificate, including scale PCs and HMIs
Retention schedule
Annual acknowledgment, including longshore workers
Annual training, OT-specific training, new personnel within 5 days of access
Untrained users supervised and recorded
Only approved hardware and software; no personal media on IT or OT; group maintenance laptops
Personal devices limited to managed email and collaboration
Bank detail changes verified through known numbers and portals
No restricted data in unapproved AI tools
